explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/1094: only finitely many (n, k) with k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 2k have least prime factor of C(n,k) greater than max(n/k, k). Floor division is harmless, because for an integer p we have p ≤ n/k iff p ≤ ⌊n/k⌋. C(n,k) ≥ 2 in this range, so minFac is a genuine prime. The ELS88 list of 14 exceptions is consistent with the finite-exceptions form.
